candidates.author: hassaanch23
candidates.subject: fix(benchmarks): correct silent answer mis-scoring in MathQA, DROP, and BBH
candidates.body:
Three cases where a *correct* prediction was scored 0 with no error raised,
systematically deflating benchmark accuracy. Each is verified by a regression
test that fails on the previous code.

1. MathQA — answer schema could not represent option "e".
   `MultipleChoiceSchemaLower` was `Literal["a","b","c","d"]`, but MathQA
   (AQuA-RAT) questions always have five options a-e ("e" is often "none of
   these"). A schema-constrained model literally cannot emit "e"
   (`MultipleChoiceSchemaLower(answer="e")` raises ValidationError), so every
   item whose gold answer is "e" (~1/5 of the dataset) was always scored 0.
   Added "e" to the schema and to the confinement instructions.

2. DROP — packing/unpacking answer spans corrupted answers containing commas.
   A golden's spans are joined into `expected_output` with a delimiter and split
   back at scoring time; the delimiter was ",", so a single-span answer like
   "1,000" round-tripped to ["1", "000"] and the correct prediction "1,000"
   could never match (`quasi_contains_score` -> 0). Switched the internal
   delimiter to the unit-separator control char, which cannot occur inside a
   DROP answer. Multi-span behavior is unchanged.

candidates.author: Kymi808
candidates.subject: Fix trimAndLoadJson corrupting valid JSON string values
candidates.body:
trimAndLoadJson stripped a comma + optional whitespace before a closing ] or }
to drop trailing commas, but it ran the regex unconditionally over the whole
string before parsing. Because it is not string-literal aware, it also rewrote
", ]" / ", }" sequences inside string values, silently corrupting valid JSON
(e.g. {"reason": "items A, B, ] done"} -> "items A, B] done"). This affects
both the metrics copy (parsing LLM judge output) and the dataset copy
(loading tool calls from CSV/JSONL).

Parse the input directly first and only apply the trailing-comma cleanup as a
fallback when that fails, so valid JSON is never altered while malformed output
with a trailing comma is still recovered. Adds regression tests covering both
copies.

candidates.subject: fix(core): registry loses live rate limiters via WeakSet structural dedup  (#2649)
candidates.body:
* fix(core): registry loses live rate limiters via WeakSet structural dedup

RateLimiterRegistry tracks live BaseRateLimiter instances per id in a
WeakSet. BaseRateLimiter.__eq__ is intentionally overridden to compare
by model fields (not identity), so the registry can find an existing
matching instance to share state with when duplicate warnings are
downgraded (GISKARD_DISABLE_DUPLICATE_RATE_LIMITERS_WARNINGS=1).

But a WeakSet is backed by a plain set, and set.add() on an element
that already compares equal (__eq__ + __hash__) to a member already in
the set is a no-op -- it does not add a second entry. So when two
structurally-equal instances share an id, only the first one is
actually stored. If that first instance is garbage collected, its
weakref removal callback empties the tracking entry entirely, even
though the second, still-alive, structurally-equal instance exists --
BaseRateLimiter.from_id() then wrongly raises "not found".

Fix: track instances in a WeakValueDictionary keyed by id(rate_limiter)
(object identity) instead of a WeakSet (structural equality via
__eq__/__hash__), so each live object gets its own slot regardless of
whether another object compares equal to it

candidates.body:
pytest resolves a relative --ignore against the invocation CWD, not the
rootdir, so giskard-scan's addopts ignores for the garak, lidar and deepteam
src trees only bit when pytest was started from inside libs/giskard-scan. Run
from the repo root (`pytest libs/giskard-scan`) they resolved to nothing, the
ignores silently missed, and --doctest-modules imported every src module:

    ERROR src/giskard/scan/integrations/garak/_generator.py
    ERROR src/giskard/scan/integrations/garak/_judge_generator.py
    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'garak'

Those three modules import garak at module level -- two of them use garak
classes as base classes, which cannot be deferred into a function body the way
_adapter.py defers its imports.

Replace the three --ignore flags with collect_ignore_glob in a lib-root
conftest.py. pytest resolves collect_ignore_glob relative to the conftest's own
directory, so the rule now holds for every invocation shape: repo root, lib
chdir, a direct src path, or an IDE runner. Keeping both mechanisms would leave
two rules for one policy, one of them CWD-dependent and silently broken.

candidates.subject: fix: strip_numeric_punctuation doesn't handle LaTeX-escaped currency symbols (#4646)
candidates.body:
* fix: strip_numeric_punctuation doesn't handle LaTeX-escaped currency symbols

Models frequently write currency amounts as "\$27.00" instead of "$27.00"
when generating inside or near LaTeX math mode, since a bare "$" would
otherwise open/close a math expression. strip_numeric_punctuation() only
strips the bare punctuation characters ($, £, €, comma, *, _), not a
backslash preceding them, so "\$27.00" is left as "\27.00" after
stripping - which fails to parse as a float and is silently rejected as
non-numeric.

This causes match(numeric=True) (location="end") to skip past the
model's actual final answer and match an earlier, unrelated number
instead when the final answer happens to be LaTeX-escaped.

Example (GSM8k, real model completion):
  "...Total Earnings = \$400 + \$60 = \$460\n$$\n\nANSWER: \$460"
  target: 460
  before: extracted "5" (from an unrelated "5 hours" earlier in the text)
  after:  extracted "460" (correct)

Fix: un-escape the backslash before the existing punctuation-stripping
regex runs. This is strictly additive - any string that already parsed
correctly has no leading backslash to strip, so no previously-correct
result can change.

Signed-off-by: Shubhra Pan

candidates.author: andrei-apollo
candidates.subject: Fix decorators return-annotation on Python 3.14 (#4554)
candidates.body:
* Fix @task/@solver/@agent return-annotation restore on Python 3.14

The decorators restore the wrapper's return annotation after
functools.wraps clobbers it by mutating wrapper.__annotations__. Under
PEP 649 (Python 3.14+) that mutation only updates the materialized
cache: functools.wraps copies the lazy __annotate__ from the wrapped
function, so any further wraps() layer — e.g. a user decorator that
extends @task and re-registers its own wrapper via registry_add —
propagates __annotate__ and silently drops the restored annotation.
create_registry_object() then sees no return annotation on the
registered callable, declines to call the factory, and returns the raw
function, so eval() fails with "'function' object has no attribute
'model'" on 3.14.

Plain assignment is not enough either: it sets __annotate__ to None,
which a further wraps() copies over the outer wrapper's own
annotations. The new set_return_annotation() helper sets both
representations — the materialized dict (all versions) and a
VALUE-format __annotate__ (3.14+) — so the annotation survives further
wrapping on every supported Python version.

* fix(scorer): return NOANSWER (not INCORRECT) when model_graded grade parser fails

When the judge's output does not match DEFAULT_GRADE_PATTERN (or a
user-supplied grade_pattern), model_graded_qa / model_graded_fact
previously returned value=INCORRECT in the else-branch of _model.py.
"Couldn't extract a verdict" and "verdict is incorrect" then became
indistinguishable in the score distribution, silently inflating the
INCORRECT count in aggregate metrics when judges flubbed the grade

when its regex fails to match, it returns NOANSWER rather than

so accuracy aggregations are unchanged; the difference is that
judge-parse failures are now distinguishable from real INCORRECTs.

* Add ci() metric for confidence intervals on the mean

candidates.author: mannemkarthik010
candidates.subject: Support itemsize-parameterized numpy dtypes in the pandas engine (#2437)
candidates.body:
Declaring a column with a sized numpy dtype raised a confusing TypeError
that named a dtype the user never wrote:

    pa.DataFrameSchema({"a": pa.Column(np.dtype("S16"))})
    TypeError: data type 'bytes128' not understood

Engine.dtype normalizes platform-specific aliases by round-tripping the
dtype through its name, so that e.g. np.intc becomes np.int32. That works
for fixed-width numeric dtypes, whose name is itself a valid dtype string,
but not for itemsize-parameterized ones: np.dtype("S16").name is
"bytes128", np.dtype("U16").name is "str512", and neither parses back.

Fall back to the dtype itself when the name does not round-trip. Its
scalar type is already platform-agnostic, so the subsequent .type lookup
resolves as it does for the unsized spelling: np.dtype("S16") now resolves
the same as bytes, and np.dtype("U16") the same as np.str_.

Note that using np_or_pd_dtype.type directly instead of the round-trip
would be simpler but silently regress the normalization this code exists
for -- np.dtype("longlong").type is np.longlong, not np.int64 -- so the
round-trip is kept and only guarded. Tests cover both directions.

Fixes #1270
